title: Minimax Design and Estimation for Matched Pairs under Bounded Pair Discordance
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded the sound delivered package subfield below the fixed field floor (paper_score_ceiling 7.2 < 7.4), with no bounded in-scope repair; field requires new research on analytic optimizer structure, cross-J superiority, or the J^-4/3 exact-minimizer Gamma limit.
gap_reasons: The exact finite result characterizes optimal designs through a very large orbit-game feasibility system rather than an analytic description of the optimizers, limiting its direct practical use.
The strict noncanonical advantage is proved only for J=2, s=1 and only against the paper-defined paired–Bernoulli segment, so it does not establish a general superiority pattern.
The advertised J^{-4/3} residual functional, Gamma limit, and exact-selection contact set remain open, as the framing acknowledges, and therefore contribute no established second-order frontier.
proof_attempt_summary: The derivation established the finite orbit-game primal/dual correspondence, an exact J=2,s=1 noncanonical rational certificate, the sharp first-order risk and limiting optimal face, and exact randomization-test inversion. It did not obtain an analytic optimizer description, a cross-J noncanonical-superiority theorem, or the proposed J^{-4/3} Gamma limit and exact-minimizer contact set; those require new research and leave the package at subfield rather than field novelty.
tldr: Known pairs are useful when their two units would respond similarly under each arm, but that two-arm similarity is latent. The integer \(s\) is therefore an analyst-selected sensitivity bound, and for every value the project jointly optimizes over all outcome-independent assignment laws and all measurable clipped SATE estimators. A pair-preserving symmetry reduction yields an exact finite conic game, a polynomial-size rational kernel, and dual certificates for the entire invariant optimal-design correspondence; an exact, nondegenerate \(J=2,s=1\) witness rules out the paper-defined paired--Bernoulli mixture workflow. The unrestricted all-design/all-estimator orbit-game layer and the \(J^{-4/3}\) second-order scale overlap with the accepted internal \texttt{exp\_multiarm\_secondorder\_minimax\_frontier\_v1} artifact. At \(K=2\), the present hard-discordance class is a structured subclass of that artifact's unrestricted binary class, coinciding with it at \(s=J\), while the pair-preserving group is a subgroup of the full unit-permutation group. The present contribution adds the hard-budget pair geometry, its joint assignment--observation pair kernel, and the exact projected optimal-design correspondence; these are not obtained by direct specialization of the full-permutation quotient, and neither a global extension nor priority is claimed. The sensitivity frontier satisfies \(J R^*(J,s_J)\to\min\{\rho,1/2\}\), while exact finite-minimizer selection on the flat first-order face remains the open \(J^{2/3}\)-critical, \(J^{-4/3}\)-residual problem.
gap: Published minimax results justify paired assignment under prognostic superpopulation structure, independent assignment under unrestricted bounded schedules, or linear shrinkage under a fixed stratified design with observed groups and bounded group CATEs. They do not solve the intermediate fixed-population sensitivity class indexed by a latent armwise pair-discordance cap while jointly choosing the design and an arbitrary measurable estimator, and they do not distinguish first-order-optimal laws from limits of exact finite minimizers.
fill: For every selected \(s\), the project supplies the correctly normalized assignment-marked orbit game, a matching least-favourable-prior dual, exact canonicality and uniqueness certificates, a strict noncanonical separation, a monotone risk sensitivity frontier, a first-order measure face, the exact-minimizer selection problem, and exact randomization-test inversion.
